hints: Notice what makes each store zero in this jump: kinetic energy needs speed $v$, elastic energy needs cord extension $x$, and gravitational energy needs height above the ground.
Recall $E_k = \frac{1}{2}mv^2$ and elastic energy $\frac{1}{2}kx^2$, so check whether the jumper is moving and whether the bungee cord is stretched at each stage.
Compare the falling stages: before the cord tightens $x = 0$, while decelerating the jumper still has speed and the cord already has extension, and at the bottom $v = 0$.
walkthrough: List the three stores: gravitational potential energy depends on height above the ground, kinetic energy depends on speed, and elastic potential energy depends on extension of the bungee cord.
On the platform the jumper has height but zero speed and the coiled cord has zero extension, so only gravitational potential energy is non-zero.
In free fall before the cord extends the jumper has height and increasing speed, so gravitational and kinetic energies are non-zero, but with zero extension the elastic energy is still zero.
At the lowest point the cord has large extension but the jumper is instantaneously stationary, so kinetic energy is zero while the other two stores can be non-zero.
Only while falling with a stretched cord and still moving downwards are height, speed and extension all non-zero at the same time. This is option C

options.A: Only gravitational potential energy is non-zero because the jumper is stationary so kinetic energy is zero and the cord is unstretched so elastic potential energy is zero.
options.B: Gravitational potential energy and kinetic energy are non-zero while falling, but elastic potential energy is zero because the cord has no extension yet.
options.C: The jumper is still above the ground, still moving, and the cord is stretched, so gravitational potential, kinetic and elastic potential energies are all non-zero.
options.D: Elastic potential energy is maximum and gravitational potential energy is still non-zero above the ground, but kinetic energy is zero because he is instantaneously stationary.
